         1       Legislative Resolution 849, memorializing the

         2       Honorable George E. Pataki, Governor, to

         3       proclaim April 9th, 1997 as Prisoner of War

         4       Recognition Day in New York State.

         5                      ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:  Senator

         6       Meier, on the resolution.

         7                      SENATOR MEIER:  Thank you, Mr.

         8       President.

         9                      Just briefly, I thought it would

        10       be appropriate for us to pause in connection

        11       with this resolution today which memorializes

        12       the Governor to proclaim April 9th as former POW

        13       Recognition Day in the state and requests that

        14       we fly the POW-MIA flag next to the state flag

        15       outside the Capitol.

        16                      The day, April 9th, is

        17       significant in connection with prisoners of war

        18       for it marks the beginning on April 9th, 1942 of

        19       the infamous Bataan Death March.  Along that

        20       march, some 11,000 American soldiers, having

        21       surrendered to the Japanese Army at Bataan, were

        22       forced to walk some 60 miles to a concentration

        23       camp, and along the way some 2,000 of them lost

        24       their lives.

        25                      But this resolution also honors







                                                             
2292

         1       all prisoners of war from all conflicts in which

         2       this country has engaged, but it focuses in on

         3       April 9th because those who participated in that

         4       march exemplified the valor and fidelity which

         5       those who were found captive while wearing the

         6       uniform of this country have shown throughout

         7       our history.

         8                      It's important today that we

         9       pause to remember those who, despite captivity

        10       and deprivation and even in some instances

        11       despite torture, kept faith with their country,

        12       kept faith with their values, kept faith with

        13       duty and honor and in doing so with all of us

        14       and with posterity.

        15                      Mr. President, I move the

        16       resolution's adoption, and I would also ask that

        17       it be opened to sponsorship to any other members

        18       wishing to do so.
